=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3256-3259 (_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When STATE_FILE is missing or unreadable, the function sets planned=0, computes floor=$((0 + ORCH_INTEGRATION_BACKPRESSURE_PROJECT_MARGIN)), and then returns max(floor, base). If an operator configures ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS below the margin (e.g. base=3, margin=5), the function returns 5 instead of the configured floor 3.
  WHY: An operator who sets ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS=3 expecting backpressure at 3 commits will instead see backpressure deferred to 5 commits when STATE_FILE is temporarily unavailable. This silently ignores the configured value on the fallback path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12759 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The backward-scan deferral log line prints "threshold=$(_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold)" — it uses the key `threshold=` to report the effective threshold while omitting the configured floor entirely.
  WHY: Log parsers or operator grep patterns scanning for `threshold=` in BACKPRESSURE_* lines expect the configured floor value. The backward-scan line breaks this convention, and the omission of the configured floor means an operator scanning logs cannot cross-reference the effective threshold against their configured value from this log line alone.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: _integration_backpressure_effective_threshold at lines 3250-3263, called at lines 3268, 3344, 3360, 12759, 13173, 13272 (plus indirectly via integration_backpressure_active_for_ahead_by at lines 3282, 3338, 12641) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The function spawns a `jq` subprocess on every call to re-read STATE_FILE, despite the result being deterministic within a single poll cycle.
  WHY: Each call forks jq to parse the state file from disk. While each individual call is cheap, the cumulative overhead in a poll cycle that already runs many gh api calls and jq operations adds latency. The state file does not change within a poll cycle, so a lazy-cached variable would reduce this to exactly one jq call.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3250-3264 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When STATE_FILE is missing or unreadable, the fallback path computes `planned=0` then adds the project margin (default 5), which can exceed the configured ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS floor. If an operator sets ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS=2 (below the default margin of 5), the function returns 5 instead of respecting the configured floor of 2.
  WHY: The intended fail-open behavior ("falls back to the configured floor when the planned count is unavailable") is not implemented. Instead, it computes a threshold from the margin even when no state exists.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3250-3252 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The helper spawns a new jq subprocess on every invocation. It is called inside hot paths: the backward-scan loop (line 12759) and the ready-to-merge loop (line 13269). Each call re-reads and re-parses the full STATE_FILE, creating O(N) overhead across multiple iterations per poll tick.
  WHY: The threshold value is deterministic within a single poll cycle, so repeated subprocess creation adds avoidable latency and CPU overhead. This is especially impactful when backpressure is active and many PRs need merge deferral.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12759 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The backward-scan deferral log uses `threshold=` to print the effective threshold value, omitting the configured floor ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS entirely.
  WHY: The contractual BACKPRESSURE_TRIGGERED/CLEARED logs correctly include both `threshold=` (the floor) and `effective_threshold=` (the additive value). This inconsistency can confuse operators and log parsers that expect `threshold=` to always represent the configured floor.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3256-3260 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When STATE_FILE is missing or unreadable, planned is set to 0, and the function computes `floor=$(( 0 + ORCH_INTEGRATION_BACKPRESSURE_PROJECT_MARGIN ))` (default 5). If an operator configures `ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS=2` (below the margin), the function returns 5 instead of respecting the configured floor of 2.
  WHY: The documented "floor" semantics are violated on state-file fallback. An operator intentionally setting a low threshold to tighten backpressure will see their configuration ignored when the state file is temporarily unavailable, potentially allowing more queued merges than intended.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3250 (inside `_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold`) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The function spawns a jq subprocess on every call, and is invoked multiple times per poll cycle in hot paths (backward-scan loop at line 12756, ready-to-merge loop, reconcile_integration_backpressure_label, BACKPRESSURE_TRIGGERED/CLEARED logs, and completion status comment generation).
  WHY: Each invocation re-reads and re-parses the full STATE_FILE. In a project with many ready-to-merge sub-issues, this creates O(N) subprocess overhead per cycle, adding unnecessary latency and CPU consumption when backpressure is active or being evaluated.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12759 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The log line uses `threshold=$(_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold)` which prints the effective threshold value, but the field name `threshold=` traditionally indicated the configured floor `ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS`. This diverges from the contractual BACKPRESSURE_TRIGGERED/BACKPRESSURE_CLEARED log format which explicitly uses both `threshold=` (configured) and `effective_threshold=` (computed).
  WHY: Log parsers and operators grepping for `threshold=` expecting the configured floor value will misinterpret the effective threshold. This inconsistency within the same script's log output format creates confusion.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold() (lines 3230-3272, especially 3245-3250) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When STATE_FILE is missing/unreadable or jq fails, `planned` falls back to 0. Then `floor=$((0 + ORCH_INTEGRATION_BACKPRESSURE_PROJECT_MARGIN))`; if this > base (ORCH_INTEGRATION_MAX_AHEAD_COMMITS), the function returns the inflated margin value instead of the configured floor.
  WHY: An operator who deliberately sets a low floor (e.g. 3) with the default margin=5 will see backpressure activate at 5 instead of 3 on any state-file transient, violating the documented "floor" contract and the intent to never let the project's own planned count self-deadlock (the regression test only exercises the happy path where STATE_FILE is present). The cross-pollination consensus (3/4 reviewers) and the Gemini/Copilot comments at line 3263 confirm the same fallback logic bug.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold() (lines 3240-3245) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: No validation or fallback path for malformed STATE_FILE JSON or jq errors beyond the silent `2>/dev/null || echo ""`; `[[ "${planned}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` then forces planned=0.
  WHY: A corrupt or truncated state comment (common in large orchestrator projects) silently produces an incorrect threshold instead of falling back safely to the configured floor. The new regression test does not exercise this path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_integration_backpressure_effective_threshold() calls (lines 1404+, 3230-3272, 12759, 13170, 13269) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The helper spawns a fresh `jq` subprocess on every invocation. It is called from hot paths: reconcile_integration_backpressure_label() (once per label reconcile), the backward-scan loop, the ready-to-merge loop, completion-status comment generation, and every deferral log line.
  WHY: In a project with many sub-issues or repeated poll ticks while backpressure is active, this adds measurable latency and CPU load per cycle (multiple full state-file parses). The four other reviewers and both Copilot/Gemini comments flagged exactly this; the lazy-cache suggestion in the review comments would eliminate it with a single run-local variable.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: BACKPRESSURE_TRIGGERED / BACKPRESSURE_CLEARED log lines (now at ~3296, ~3312, 12759) and backward-scan deferral message (12759) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The contractual stable log prefixes keep `threshold=` but now emit the *effective* value (or a mixed message). The completion-status comment and deferral logs also changed wording without preserving the old phrasing as an alias.
  WHY: Log parsers, drift-audit, workflow-log-analysis, and operator greps that keyed on the exact previous format (documented in agents.md "Stable log prefixes") will break or produce false positives. The PR claims "the contractual BACKPRESSURE_TRIGGERED/CLEARED lines keep threshold= and additively gain effective_threshold=" but the implementation overwrote the value in several places.
